svg.text: SOCIAL NETWORK — THE NEWSFEED READ PATH
getNewsfeed(userId, limit) — two filters, then a Strategy
① RESOLVE THE VIEWER
User viewer = getUser(userId); // else UserNotFoundException
the viewer carries the graph — friendIds, followingIds, blockedUserIds
② VISIBILITY FILTER — isVisibleToUser(post, viewer)
evaluated in this exact order, and the order is the design:
if (blockedEitherWay(viewer, post.getAuthorId())) return false; // BLOCK WINS
if (visibility == PUBLIC) return true;
if (authorId.equals(viewer.getUserId())) return true; // your own post
if (visibility == FRIENDS_ONLY) return viewer.isFriend(authorId);
a block outranks even a PUBLIC post — the safety rule must be checked FIRST ✓
③ THE STRATEGY — feedAlgorithm.generateFeed(viewer, posts, limit)
ChronologicalFeedAlgorithm does two more things:
.filter(p -> viewer.getUserId().equals(p.getAuthorId())
|| viewer.isFriend(p.getAuthorId())
|| viewer.isFollowing(p.getAuthorId())) // RELEVANCE
.sorted(newest first).limit(limit)
CAN I see it (service) vs SHOULD I see it (strategy) — two separate questions ✓
④ RETURN — newest-first, capped at limit
swap in EngagementFeedAlgorithm or MlRankedFeedAlgorithm: nothing else changes
WHAT THIS COSTS TODAY — say it before you're asked
There is no posts-by-author index. Step ② streams EVERY post in the system
on every feed request: O(all posts × friend-set lookup) per call.
The double filter also means a post is tested twice — once for visibility in the
service, once for relevance in the strategy.
Correct and readable at demo scale; hopeless at real scale. The fix is on the right.
FAN-OUT: THE FOLLOW-UP YOU WILL GET
PULL ON READ (what this code does)
On every getNewsfeed: gather the author set, scan posts, rank.
+ writes are cheap — createPost touches one map
+ no stale feed, no reconciliation, no duplicate storage
+ unfollow / block take effect instantly
− reads are expensive, and reads vastly outnumber writes
− cost grows with TOTAL content, not with what you follow
right for a demo, and right for users who follow thousands of accounts
PUSH ON WRITE (fan-out)
On createPost: append the post id to every follower's feed list.
+ reads become O(limit) — just take the head of a precomputed list
+ ranking can be done offline, asynchronously
− a celebrity post is millions of writes ("the fan-out problem")
− feeds are duplicated storage, and go stale on unfollow/block
− deleting a post means chasing it through N feeds
block must still be re-checked at read time, or a block wouldn't hide old posts
THE HYBRID — the expected answer
Fan out on write for normal users. Their follower count is small,
so the write amplification is bounded.
Keep celebrities on pull. Above a follower threshold, don't fan out —
merge their recent posts in at read time.
A read then = precomputed feed ∪ celebrity pull, merged and re-ranked ✓
FeedAlgorithm stays the same interface either way — that's why it's a Strategy
THE CHEAPEST FIRST STEP IN THIS CODEBASE
Add postsByAuthor: Map<authorId, List<postId>>. The feed then walks
friends ∪ following instead of every post in the system — one index,
and getUserPosts() stops being an O(all posts) scan too ✓
WHAT FEEDS THE FEED — the three graph writes
FRIENDSHIP — mutual, two-sided, consent required
sendFriendRequest(a, b) — rejects self, blocked, duplicate, already-friends
acceptFriendRequest(requestId, accepterId) — the actor id is load-bearing
requireRequestFor() throws UnauthorizedException unless the responder
IS the receiver — otherwise the sender could befriend anyone unilaterally.
accept() then writes friendIds on BOTH users, in one call.
requirePending() makes answering twice throw — ACCEPTED and REJECTED are terminal ✓
the duplicate-request check streams all requests AND is check-then-act
FOLLOW — asymmetric, no consent, still two writes
follow(followerId, followeeId):
follower.follow(followeeId); // followingIds
followee.addFollower(followerId); // followerIds
Two sets, kept in sync by hand — the classic place a graph drifts.
not atomic: a crash between the two lines leaves a one-way edge
a real store makes this one edge row, or one transaction
BLOCK — the rule that outranks everything else
blockUser(a, b) also tears down the existing friendship.
requireNotBlocked() is symmetric — if EITHER side blocked the other,
nothing passes. It guards sendMessage, likePost, commentOnPost,
sendFriendRequest — and isVisibleToUser checks it before anything else.
Storing a block without consulting it makes the feature decorative.
That is a safety bug, not a cosmetic one — the sentence worth saying out loud.
a blocked user must not learn they are blocked from the error message either
MESSAGES — a canonical pair key, same trick as the feed
conversationId = sorted(userA, userB).join("_") ⇒ (a,b) and (b,a) collide.
conversations: CHM<convId, CopyOnWriteArrayList<Message>>
a plain ArrayList inside a ConcurrentHashMap dropped ~8% of messages —
a mistake that LOOKS thread-safe because the outer map is.
COW is right here (few messages read often); wrong for an unbounded chat history
SAY IT OUT LOUD:
"Visibility is a safety question and belongs in the service; relevance is a product question and belongs in the Strategy. Block is checked first, because a block outranks a PUBLIC post."
FRIEND vs FOLLOW — the distinction the whole graph turns on

Friend = mutual, requires an accept, unlocks FRIENDS_ONLY posts, and is removable from either side. Follow = one-sided, needs no consent, only ever unlocks PUBLIC posts. Both feed the newsfeed; only one gates visibility.
LEGEND

g.text: Patterns on this path: Strategy (FeedAlgorithm) · guard-first visibility · canonical pair key (conversations) · defensive copies on every getter
Honest gaps: no posts-by-author index · double filtering · follow's two writes are not atomic · User's sets are plain HashSets
